newsitem.title: FRANCE: Airlines eye Lufthansa on fuel surcharge.
newsitem.headline: Airlines eye Lufthansa on fuel surcharge.

text.p: Air France Cargo has no plans to withdraw its cargo fuel surcharge on April 15, a spokeswoman told Reuters.

She was commenting on the announcement earlier today by Lufthansa Cargo that it was dropping the 10 US cents per kg air cargo fuel surcharge introduced on November 1 to meet sharply higher jet fuel costs.
A spokesman in London for British Airways World Cargo said: "the surcharge is under review but there is no change at this moment in time."
BA introduced a six pence per kg increase on November 8 on intercontinental freight rates and three pence on European and UK routes.
Meanwhile a Swisscargo official said he could say nothing specific today but a statement on the surcharge was expected tomorrow, April 11.
The round of surcharges applied by many airlines since last November reflected the sharp rises in the price of jet fuel since July 1995.

Delta Airlines, United Airlines and Virgin Atlantic have already dropped the surcharge and the air cargo industry has been awaiting a similar move by one of the top European cargo carriers. KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV confirmed earlier this week that it had told the Dutch shippers' organisation it expected to lift the surcharge on April 15 unless there was sudden upturn in the oil price. -Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+44 171 542-5017
